# flotilla

> A small platform for agent fleets: flotillad (Go) schedules routines, keeps cases, the ledger and the operator UI, and dispatches each run to a worker (Python, in Docker, on the host or a remote machine). The fleets: triage (alerts and errors to GitHub issues), bugfix (an issue to a draft fix), ops (backups and host checks), SEO, and platform checks.

Rules for coding agents are in AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md imports it); bugfix-fleet/AGENTS.md is scoped to that folder. Decisions are ADRs under docs/adr/ and proposals RFCs under docs/rfc/; how the system fits together is docs/architecture/; how to run each fleet is docs/operations/. Each routine is a spec in fleets/<fleet>/<routine>.yaml, or a folder fleets/<fleet>/<routine>/ with a routine.yaml and its versions (v1/spec.yaml).

This file is generated by scripts/llms_txt.py from llms.config.json; `make llms-txt` rewrites it and `make lint` (CI) fails when it is stale.

## Agent rules

- [Project overview](AGENTS.md#project-overview): flotilla is a plain, spec-driven platform for small fleets of AI agents.
- [Stack](AGENTS.md#stack)
- [Project-specific rules](AGENTS.md#project-specific-rules): Never commit secrets, the ledger, findings, fleet data, production payloads, or environment
- [Code layout](AGENTS.md#code-layout): Imported from the installation's ops repo at `f0ed072` with their history (`git filter-repo`), without
- [Domain knowledge](AGENTS.md#domain-knowledge): The fleets being migrated came from the installation's ops repo: `fleetd/`, `signal-fleet/`,
- [Named ADR anchors](AGENTS.md#named-adr-anchors): ADR-0001 — Platform foundations: read first.
- [Where to look](AGENTS.md#where-to-look): Active session log: `docs/history/` (latest file = current state).
- [What overrides this file](AGENTS.md#what-overrides-this-file): Direct instruction in chat: a one-shot ask supersedes a default.
- [bugfix-fleet/AGENTS.md](bugfix-fleet/AGENTS.md): rules scoped to the bugfix-fleet folder (the bake-off era code)

## Architecture

- [Context](docs/architecture/context.md): flotilla runs small fleets of AI agents for one operator.
- [Data](docs/architecture/data.md): The public repo ships examples with placeholder values.
- [A case, end to end](docs/architecture/run-lifecycle.md): Every problem flotilla handles is a case: detected, diagnosed, handed to the routine that can fix it, planned, approved …

## By area (code folder: what to read before changing it)

- [cmd/, internal/ (flotillad, Go)](docs/architecture/components.md): the components and how they talk; then [data](docs/architecture/data.md) for the store and [run lifecycle](docs/architecture/run-lifecycle.md) for a run's path
- [internal/ui/ (operator UI)](DESIGN.md): the design system; the product it serves is [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md), the decision [ADR-0014](docs/adr/ADR-0014-operator-ui.md)
- [internal/mcpserver/](docs/operations/mcp.md): the MCP server: tools, tokens, how other agents use it
- [internal/slackconn/](docs/operations/slack.md): the Slack connector
- [signal-fleet/mvp/ (the triage fleet's code)](signal-fleet/mvp/README.md): the cycle code; the fleet's design is [signal-fleet/README.md](signal-fleet/README.md) and its north star [SIGNALS.md](signal-fleet/SIGNALS.md); the model's playbook is [fleets/triage/playbooks/triage.md](fleets/triage/playbooks/triage.md)
- [bugfix/ (the bugfix fleet)](docs/operations/bugfix.md): running it; the design is [RFC-0010](docs/rfc/RFC-0010-bugfix-on-the-platform.md), the threat model [SR-0001](docs/security-reviews/SR-0001-bugfix-coding-harness.md)
- [seo/ (the sites example's code)](docs/rfc/RFC-0012-seo-fleet.md): the site checks; the example fleet is [fleets/sites](fleets/sites)
- [runtime/ (model client, harness, skills, ledger)](docs/rfc/RFC-0002-job-runtime.md): the job runtime the routines run on; the decision is [ADR-0004](docs/adr/ADR-0004-job-runtime.md)
- [ops/ (the ops fleet)](docs/rfc/RFC-0009-post-incident-review.md): case review; host actions are [ADR-0006](docs/adr/ADR-0006-node-agent.md)
- [deploy/ (installing on a host)](deploy/compose/README.md): the compose stack, config and secrets on the host; remote workers are [deploy/remote/README.md](deploy/remote/README.md), the whole picture [deployment](docs/architecture/deployment.md)
- [getting started](docs/development.md): from a clone to `make demo`, the gates, where things are
- [tests (every area)](docs/testing.md): the test tiers and what each make target runs
- [Makefile](Makefile): every gate: `make ci-fast` (lint, unit tests) on every push, `make replay` (the triage replays, needs the private corpora), `make test-e2e`, `make docs-lint`

## By service (what a triage agent needs)

- [flotillad](docs/architecture/deployment.md): GlitchTip project `flotilla` (its own ERROR logs, environment operations); container `flotillad`
- [workers and egress on the host](deploy/compose/README.md): containers `flotilla-worker-<role>` (triage, ops-read, ops-act-host, marketing, triage-candidate) and `flotilla-egress`, `flotilla-egress-seo`; the triage fleet's logs and metrics carry service `triage-fleet` (the candidate `triage-fleet-candidate`)
- [remote workers (bugfix on a second machine)](deploy/remote/README.md): containers `flotilla-remote-*`, linked to flotillad over the tailnet
- [host agents](docs/operations/host-keys.md): container `flotilla-hosts`: host actions and their keys

## Decisions (ADRs)

- [ADR-0001 — Platform foundations](docs/adr/ADR-0001-platform-foundations.md): Accepted
- [ADR-0002 — Run flotilla in Docker, one worker per fleet](docs/adr/ADR-0002-run-in-docker.md): Accepted. ADR-0001 puts flotilla on the host, as the `claude` account.
- [ADR-0003 — Dependencies, spec format and base images for flotillad](docs/adr/ADR-0003-dependencies-and-images.md): Accepted. Phase 2 builds flotillad (RFC-0001 §9).
- [ADR-0004 — The job runtime: five core concepts](docs/adr/ADR-0004-job-runtime.md): Accepted. Phase 3 builds the job runtime and moves the triage fleet onto it.
- [ADR-0005 — The agent pipeline: cases, capabilities, recall, policy and the actuator](docs/adr/ADR-0005-agent-pipeline.md): Accepted. ADR-0004 gave flotilla's job runtime its core concepts, shaped around triage.
- [ADR-0006 — The flotilla node agent: host actions and connectors, on any host](docs/adr/ADR-0006-node-agent.md): Accepted. ADR-0005 needs host writes (restart a container, rerun a backup job) to run through a privileged component on each …
- [ADR-0007 — "Routine" replaces "job"](docs/adr/ADR-0007-routine.md): Accepted. Amended by ADR-0020 (2026-11-18): a routine has versions (live, shadow, previous, retired), each worked by its …
- [ADR-0008 — One autonomy scale: shadow, propose, auto](docs/adr/ADR-0008-autonomy.md): Accepted
- [ADR-0009 — Host agent names: workers think, host agents act](docs/adr/ADR-0009-host-agent-names.md): Accepted. ADR-0006 named the program flotilla installs on each host in several ways: "host agent" in prose, `flotilla-node` as …
- [ADR-0010 — Memory and knowledge, not "recall"](docs/adr/ADR-0010-memory-and-knowledge.md): Accepted. ADR-0004 named two of the runtime's core concepts memory (what flotilla recorded) and external knowledge (what exists …
- [ADR-0011 — Tools and actions, not "capabilities"](docs/adr/ADR-0011-tools-and-actions.md): Accepted. "Capability" meant two things.
- [ADR-0012 — Skills in the harness](docs/adr/ADR-0012-skills.md): Accepted. Skills (a `SKILL.md` folder of know-how, the format Claude Code and opencode read) let an agent pull in instructions …
- [ADR-0013 — Fleet packs](docs/adr/ADR-0013-fleet-packs.md): Accepted. A fleet's behaviour lives more and more in text: routine specs, playbooks, skills, harness settings.
- [ADR-0014 — The operator UI, users and roles](docs/adr/ADR-0014-operator-ui.md): Accepted. The operator works flotilla from a terminal, which is not possible on a phone.
- [ADR-0015 — The MCP server](docs/adr/ADR-0015-mcp-server.md): Accepted. Other agents (Claude sessions, the second machine's assistant) had no way into flotilla but SSH and the container's CLI …
- [ADR-0016 — Post-incident review](docs/adr/ADR-0016-post-incident-review.md): Accepted. The first shadow case was the chain right within a wrong check (a 20 h threshold on a ~24 h backup), and nothing in …
- [ADR-0017 — Routine actions](docs/adr/ADR-0017-routine-actions.md): Accepted. The registry had two executors.
- [ADR-0018 — Harness parts: the system prompt, unknown tools and hooks](docs/adr/ADR-0018-harness-parts.md): Accepted. The industry names the parts of an agent's harness: the model, the system prompt, the tools, the hooks around tool …
- [ADR-0019 — Durable runs: a checkpoint, and a resume flotillad allows](docs/adr/ADR-0019-durable-runs.md): Accepted. A bugfix run takes minutes to an hour and spends money in model calls.
- [ADR-0020 — Routine versions, stations and harnesses](docs/adr/ADR-0020-routine-versions-stations-harnesses.md): Accepted. The operator, 2026-11-18: changing a business process means shipping a new version of its routine.
- [ADR-0021 — The examples catalogue, and run tokens required by default](docs/adr/ADR-0021-examples-catalogue-and-run-tokens-default.md): Accepted. Step 5 moved the example fleets to the v2 format (a folder per routine, `routine.yaml` plus `v1/`), put triage's cycle …

- [RFC-0008 — The MCP server: other agents see and steer flotilla](docs/rfc/RFC-0008-mcp-server.md): Accepted → ADR-0015. flotilla has a CLI for the operator on the host and a UI for people.

- [RFC-0011 — Remote workers: routines on any machine, the host orchestrating](docs/rfc/RFC-0011-remote-workers.md): Accepted. Every worker runs today on the host, beside flotillad, on its internal Docker network.
- [RFC-0013 — The clarifier: answering "needs info" before the fix, and asking once](docs/rfc/RFC-0013-bugfix-clarifier.md): Accepted. The first four PR plans were judged by the operator and the fleet session on 2026-11-16: one right (#648), one partial …
- [RFC-0014 — The visual plane and mashups: flotilla seen live, and as the governed step in business processes](docs/rfc/RFC-0014-visual-plane-and-mashups.md): Draft. Two ideas, one aim: that people trust agents with real work because they can see what the agents do and how they are …
